item.title: Kyle Juszczyk responds to beer fine by explaining in detail his celebration is about his nickname – Juice
item.description: Kyle Juszczyk says his touchdown celebration is about drinking juice, not beer, and George Kittle jokingly wants to change his teammate's nickname.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL unwittingly waded into a silly back-and-forth with Kyle Juszczyk on Thursday by fining him over a touchdown celebration that it says imitates "chugging a beer" which the league finds offensive while but San Francisco 49ers fullback has a pretty convincing explanation for:

"Man, I feel like there's already been so much put out there," Juszczyk said while facing a scrum of reporters around his locker stall. "I don't know how else to say it. I wasn't drinking beer in my celebration.

"I think you guys all know my nickname is 'Juice.' I have juice [inscribed] on my pads, and the stadium yells, 'Juice' when I catch the ball.

NFL FINES PLAYER NICKNAMED 'JUICE' $14,926 FOR USING A DRINKING CELEBRATION, CALLING IT OFFENSIVE

"When I celebrate, I celebrate by drinking juice and it's been that way for years."

That wasn't the NFL's interpretation when it sent Juszczyk an email telling him he's being fined $14,926 for what it described as, "an offensive demonstration" that could "reasonably be construed as being in poor taste."

NEW NFL FINE SCHEDULE IS GOING TO A POINT SYSTEM THAT COULD LEAD TO SUSPENSIONS BUT ALSO REFUNDS

The celebration in question includes Juszczyk raising his hand to his mouth and acting as if he's drinking something.

The league immediately decided Juszczyk was imitating drinking beer.

"That's the other side of it, is I don't even drink beer," Juszczyk said. "I may be drinking like five times a year and always in the offseason, and it's usually with [teammate] George [Kittle] because he peer pressures me."

Kittle, by the way, found this whole episode quite funny. Maybe because it's ridiculous.

Anyway, the tight end has called Juszczyk by his nickname for years. But know he's going to change that.

"I think we're going to sign a petition," Kittle said. "Juice's new nickname is Beer now."

Niners quarterback quarterback Brock Purdy doesn't understand the fine because Juszczyk has been doing his drinking celebration for years and never been fined for it before.

"Yeah, I've seen Juice do his celebration for like five years," Purdy said. "So I'm a little confused about that punishment he's dealing with."

Purdy said head coach Kyle Shanahan has warned the players about violent acts in their celebrations or jumping on the goal post — looking at you, Stefon Diggs – but never has the Juszczyk celebration been mentioned.

"Juice, that's his name, he drinks a juice box after scoring a touchdown," Purdy said. "We're all confused and it [stinks] to be honest for him."

This also kind of [stinks]: Juszczyk said he didn't find out from the league first. Shanahan found out first and told him early Thursday morning.

"When Kyle told me that during breakfast, I thought maybe he was just messing with me," Juszczyk said. "But it's real."

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Look, the NFL has rules and some apply to improper celebrations. But to jump to conclusions that the intent of this celebration was to drink alcohol and specifically beer was a leap.

(Maybe not a leap from a league that is awash in beer sponsorships).

Juszczyk confirmed he is appealing, as OutKick reported earlier. The appeal hearing is scheduled for Tuesday via Zoom.

item.title: Michigan nurse accused of breaking bones and bruising premature infant at children's hospital
item.description: Kieran Ansley allegedly left a premature baby with broken bones and bruises at Helen DeVos Children's Hospital, entering her room 27 times that night.
item.content:encoded:
A nurse is accused of beating a prematurely born 4-month-old baby girl at a Michigan hospital, leaving the infant with broken bones and bruises, including injuries to her tongue, according to reports.

Kieran Ansley, 43, who was fired from Helen DeVos Children’s Hospital in Grand Rapids, is charged with multiple counts of child abuse.

The child was born four months premature but was making progress after spending months in the ICU and was expected to go home in April, WOOD-TV reported.

TEXAS DENTIST ACCUSED OF FATAL MISTAKES AFTER 4-YEAR-OLD DIES DURING DENTAL PROCEDURE

"She was born at 23 weeks: 1 pound, 1 ounce," her grandfather, Robert Steavens, told WOOD-TV. "And she made it through her due date, ready to go home. And then two days before she was ready to go home, this happened."

The girl's mother visited her on April 2. As she approached the room, Ansley "‘jogged’ to cut them off before getting to the room, telling them that the infant had ‘slept through the night,’" court records show.

MARYLAND DAD BLAMED 'SATAN' AFTER 2-MONTH-OLD DAUGHTER DIED FROM HORRIFIC HEAD TRAUMA

The mother also noticed that the infant's tongue was "blue and black" and that several bruises were on the child that weren't there the night before.

Court records show Ansley claimed to have "seen this in the past and it was not a big deal," court records show.

During an investigation, one hospital staffer said Ansley "seemed flustered" and "a little bit frustrated" that night. Ansley was also described as being "scatterbrained."

OHIO DAYCARE WORKER CONVICTED OF HORRIFIC PHYSICAL ABUSE OF TODDLERS SENTENCED TO YEARS IN PRISON

Others recalled Ansley being "heated" and "overwhelmed," court records show.

A staff log from the night the infant was allegedly abused showed 32 instances in which someone entered the baby’s room. Ansley accounted for 27 of those visits, the records show, the news station reported.

Fox News Digital reached out to Ansley's attorney and the hospital for comment.

Defense attorney Damian Nunzio told the news outlet that Ansley has been cooperative during the investigation, spent "many years" working with ICU patients, and is a "very good person."

"And we are confident that our investigation will let the truth come to light," Nunzio added.

Ansley, who was released on bond and is expected to appear in court on Nov. 10, was fired after the allegations came to light.

The child, now 10 months old, is at home and "doing wonderful," Steavens said.

"We’ve been blessed, and we’ve watched the baby grow," he continued. "We’re trusting in God and healing as a family and trusting the process will move forward."

item.title: Xi can’t escape protesters’ cries at deafening dinner demonstration
item.description: Protesters chanting "Free Hong Kong" and demanding freedom for political prisoners were heard over Trump's State Dinner welcoming Xi Jinping.
item.content:encoded:
Audible protests blared over President Donald Trump and first lady Melania Trump’s welcome to Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, at the White House Thursday night, at times drowning out the State Dinner event.

"Free Hong Kong," "Xi Jinping you’re not welcome" and "freedom for political prisoners" were among the chants shouted.

Protestors gathered across the Northern portico in Lafeyette Park to stand against the communist leader’s visit, where the two leaders are expected to discuss artificial intelligence and intellectual property theft, trade practices and rare-earth minerals.

TRUMP-XI REUNION COMES WITH UNFINISHED BUSINESS — AND A BIGGER BATTLE LOOMING

The chants could be heard clearly before the Marine Corps band began playing and remained audible, though less prominently, throughout the performance.

Tibetan, Uyghur, Hong Kong democracy, Chinese pro-democracy and Falun Gong groups gathered in Washington this week to call attention to the Chinese government’s alleged human rights abuses.

President Trump has previously referred to Chinese President Xi Jinping as "Pooh Bear," a nickname rooted in an online meme comparing Xi to Winnie the Pooh. Protesters leaned into the comparison Thursday, dressing as the cartoon bear during a demonstration outside the White House.

The dinner had 134 guests, including the two leaders and prominent tech CEOs such as Jensen Huang of NVIDIA, Mark Zuckerberg of Meta, Lisa Su of AMD, Tim Cook of Apple, Sam Altman of OpenAI, Elon Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, Jeff Bezos of Amazon, Satya Nadella of Microsoft, Sundar Pichai of Google and TikTok CEO Shou Zi Chew.

TRUMP SHOULD PRESS XI ON CHINA’S PERSECUTION OF BELIEVERS AT HOME AND ABROAD

Many demonstrators have called for the release of political prisoners, including House Speaker Mike Johnson, who has called for the release of Dr. Gulshan Abbas.

Abbas is a retired Uyghur doctor, who disappeared from her home in China on Sept. 10, 2018. Chinese officials later sentenced her to 20 years in prison on terrorism-related charges that her family calls fabricated.

XI PREPARES CHINA ‘FOR BATTLE’ AS EXPERT WARNS OF GRAVE DANGER FACING US AHEAD OF DC SUMMIT

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House to see if her release, or others, are on the negotiating table during this visit.

Famous American tenor Christopher Macchio, who was featured at the Republican National Convention in Dallas a few weeks ago, will entertain for the evening, along with military musicians from the Army and the Marine Corps.

After the dinner, both presidents are expected to retire for the evening ahead of their visit to the National Archives Friday.

item.title: Iranian president blames US for Middle East conflict while denying nuclear ambitions, offers to dilute uranium
item.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian claims Tehran will submit its nuclear program to verification and dilute enriched uranium to ease tensions.
item.content:encoded:
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian flatly denied Thursday that Tehran wants a nuclear bomb while claiming Iran is willing to submit its nuclear program for international inspection, blaming Washington for the nearly seven-month war in the Middle East and accusing it of blocking diplomacy.

Asked point-blank during an exclusive interview on Fox News’ "Special Report," "Do you want a nuclear bomb or not?" Pezeshkian firmly rejected the premise.

"Not at all. Not at all. Our martyred, esteemed supreme leader had announced several times that from a religious decree, it is unholy. It is illegal," he told Brett Baier, referencing religious edicts issued against weapons of mass destruction.

IRAN 'ALREADY AGREED' TO GIVING UP NUCLEAR WEAPON AMBITIONS, TRUMP REVEALS

The Iranian leader's public denial came amid long-term international scrutiny of Iran’s nuclear program and its enrichment of uranium to levels well beyond those typically used for civilian nuclear power.

This, in fact, became President Donald Trump's central rationale for launching Operation Epic Fury back in February.

On Thursday, however, Pezeshkian went on to indicate that Tehran would be open to lowering its enrichment levels and allowing outside verification as part of an effort to ease nuclear tensions.

"So that weapon's mass destruction. We said we’re willing to dilute them. It’s not a big deal. We are willing to submit ourselves to verification," he said.

Pezeshkian also pointed to the failed memorandum of understanding, or MOU, signed by himself and President Donald Trump in June that was intended to halt hostilities and establish a framework for a broader U.S.-Iran agreement.

The process was intended by Washington to lead to an end to Iran’s nuclear ambitions and included a 60-day process toward that final agreement.

"We have no problems. We did reach an agreement with your president," Pezeshkian said of President Donald Trump, who signed the agreement.

"That agreement was signed, and based on that, we are willing and still wish to move forward," he claimed.

IRAN NUCLEAR DEAL HINGES ON IAEA ACCESS TO LONG-BLOCKED ATOMIC WEAPON SITES, EXPERTS SAY

"And the framework was agreed upon. We had not closed the Strait of Hormuz; it was open, without any legal justification or framework," he said.

"They attacked us. They assassinated and martyred our esteemed supreme leader, our scientists are military commanders and government."

Pezeshkian went on to criticize Washington for the subsequent breakdown in diplomacy but insisted Tehran remains prepared to reach an agreement.

"The problem is that America, instead of conducting dialog, they descend into the arena by bombing us first, by blocking every pathway. We are ready," he said.

"This is not the way to conduct yourself on the world stage. They can have free access to see whatever we have, but not to put us under such pressure, under blockades, deny us access."

Pezeshkian also placed broader blame on Washington for the war.

"We do not seek to kill Americans, as shown by actions, demonstrable actions. America has sought to kill Iranians," Pezeshkian said before adding: "What we know is that if we’re attacked, we must defend ourselves."

TRUMP BETS ECONOMIC PRESSURE CAN SQUEEZE IRAN AS REGIME’S OWN FAILURES DEEPEN THE PAIN

Addressing U.S. military strikes — including Operation Outcast — and increasing secondary sanctions, Pezeshkian said Iran would continue resisting Washington’s campaign.

"This is something that has been the doing of the United States," he said. "We will keep resisting. We will find ways, and the life of our country will continue. We will remain."

"Yes, we do have economic issues, certainly. But in order to remain, we will go through any hardship and endure," he said of Iran.

"If America thinks that they can keep sanctioning us, we have nothing to do, nor do we consider any type of American elections. If the current American government, within international legal frameworks, wishes to reach an agreement, fine. If not, before the elections or after the elections, what difference does it make for us?"

Pezeshkian repeated that Iran does not want the war to continue, while blaming Israel for helping provoke the conflict and putting responsibility on Washington to bring it to an end.

TRUMP GIVES EVERY NATION AN EASY CHOICE: DO BUSINESS WITH AMERICA OR TERRORIST IRAN

"We will stand resolutely to defend ourselves. We never sought war. We do not seek war," he said.

"I deeply believe that humans should not cause the death of another human. But with the instigations conducted by Israel, they have imposed this war on us.

"But we do not wish to continue. It’s America that must choose whether it wants to end this or not."

The Iranian president also addressed reports that Iranian forces used Chinese satellite imagery to carry out a deadly strike on a U.S. base in Jordan. The attack resulted in the deaths of three U.S. service members.

When questioned about the reports, Pezeshkian denied direct knowledge.

"I’m specifically unaware of these purported images that you talk about," Pezeshkian said. 

"Now, what do militaries do with one another between two countries? It is their own business within their own guidelines," he insisted.

item.title: Meet 'the devil': Actor who plays Satan, Judas Iscariot shares power of comedy in uncertain political times
item.description: Jarret LeMaster has played Satan and Adolf Hitler but now voices Bumblebee in the Transformers 40th anniversary short alongside Frank Welker.
item.content:encoded:
Jarret LeMaster has played some sinister roles as Satan, Adolf Hitler and Judas Iscariot, but now he's stepping into one of pop culture's most beloved franchises as Bumblebee.

The Christian actor, writer and former worship leader voices the Autobots in "Optimus Prime: Awakening," the new animated short accompanying the 40th anniversary theatrical rerelease of "The Transformers: The Movie."

But LeMaster told Fox News Digital there is one thing he would rather not do on camera: kiss another woman.

"I don't wanna kiss anybody, and, so, playing bad guys makes a lot of sense for me," LeMaster said. "They never kiss anybody, you know. They just murder them.

BILLY BALDWIN ADMITS HE REFUSED TO KISS CO-STAR AFTER WEEKS OF TENSION ON SET

"When you're murdering somebody, you're always pretending," he continued. "When you're kissing someone, you are always actually kissing them. And, so, you know, that's my line. I don't wanna cross that line.

"Playing bad guys really works for my family," he joked. "And then my kids can look up to me as a great villain."

It's an unusual résumé for someone who spent years working in church ministry.

LeMaster said he still volunteers and leads worship at his local church, although he tends to keep some of his acting work "on the DL."

SKILLET’S JOHN COOPER SAYS CHRISTIANS WHO CALL ROCK MUSIC ‘DEMONIC’ ARE ‘GETTING THE GOSPEL WRONG’

"Sometimes people are upset that I play 'Woke Jesus.' Sometimes people think that it's weird that I played the devil. Sometimes people were offended that I would, you know, play Adolf Hitler," he said. "The one that is not offensive is Bumblebee. People are very excited about that for some reason."

LeMaster's path from church ministry to professional villain began when he got a call one day asking him to play a Russian murderer in a sketch for Christian satire outlet The Babylon Bee.

"We need a Russian murderer. You kind of look like that," LeMaster recalled being told.

At the time, he was working full time at his church and with the Bee. He initially assumed the company must be based somewhere like "Idaho or Narnia," only to discover it was in California.

'THE PASSION OF THE CHRIST' RETURNS TO THEATERS IN 4K WITH A 'RESURRECTION OF THE CHRIST' SNEAK PEEK

One villain eventually led to another.

"I don't know why I always get cast as bad characters," LeMaster said. "I think it's probably just because I'm bald. ... I blame the media. I blame [actor] Jason Statham."

His latest role puts LeMaster firmly on the other side of the good-versus-evil divide.

"Optimus Prime: Awakening" features LeMaster as Bumblebee alongside Frank Welker as Megatron and Soundwave and the late Peter Cullen as Optimus Prime. The short accompanies a 40th anniversary rerelease that exceeded initial box-office projections, prompting additional theatrical dates through Oct. 7.

LeMaster said he initially underestimated the significance of the project because director Josh Wassung was a friend.

FROM DISNEY MAGIC TO ANCIENT FAITH: DAVID HENRIE ON WHY GEN Z IS FLOCKING TO CHURCH

"I thought this was my friend's little movie, this little Transformers movie that he was making for Hasbro," he said.

Then he learned Cullen was involved. LeMaster praised the longtime Optimus Prime actor for embodying "strength and gentleness and kindness" and "protecting the weak."

"Who am I? Why do I get to play Bumblebee?" LeMaster recalled wondering.

For LeMaster, even the Transformers role connects back to his faith.

"It's an opportunity to sort of spread good news in the kingdom through, you know, robots," he said.

And despite joining the Autobots, LeMaster admitted Satan remains particularly fun to play.

"I love playing the devil because he is so much like me," he said. "I know that sounds really weird."

His Babylon Bee version of Satan is less fire-and-brimstone than frustrated corporate middle management.

"What if the devil was an HR director?" LeMaster said.

"You know, guys, it's been a rough quarter," he said in character. "Make sure that you put cover letters on all the things you turn in, please."

Beneath the joke is a serious approach to portraying villains. LeMaster said he looks for something good in a character's motivations and then considers how it became distorted.

"There's nothing that the devil can create in and of himself. He can only take what's good, and he can twist it," he said.

"You always start with a good guy, and then you can twist it to something evil," LeMaster added. "That's kind of what I think the best villains end up being like."

item.title: Turning Point USA fires back at ICE shooting lawyer over deleted Charlie Kirk post
item.description: Turning Point USA's Andrew Kolvet called the ICE shooting victim and his attorney a "perfect match" after her deleted post about Charlie Kirk resurfaced.
item.content:encoded:
Turning Point USA (TPUSA) spokesman Andrew Kolvet fired back Thursday at the attorney representing a Venezuelan man shot by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer in Austin, Texas, calling the two a "perfect match" after the lawyer drew criticism over a deleted social media post referencing the assassination of conservative activist Charlie Kirk.

Kolvet, also executive producer of "The Charlie Kirk Show," told Fox News Digital the organization backed the federal immigration officers involved while criticizing attorney Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch and her client, 28-year-old Wilber Rafael Garces Perez.

"We stand with our brave men and women of ICE who are defending American sovereignty and keeping American citizens safe," Kolvet said. "While everyone is entitled to their defense, it's not surprising the quality of lawyer an illegal alien from Venezuela attracts who had a final notice of deportation before leading law enforcement on a dangerous high-speed chase.

"They seem a perfect match."

REMEMBERING CHARLIE KIRK: TURNING POINT USA'S ANDREW KOLVET REFLECTS ON CONSERVATIVE GROUP'S CHALLENGING YEAR

Lincoln-Goldfinch drew criticism this week after a since-deleted social media post referencing Kirk resurfaced. In the post, she questioned how someone could resist being shot while invoking Kirk.

"How do you resist getting shot in the neck? Does Charlie Kirk have any advice on that?" Lincoln-Goldfinch said in the post.

She previously addressed the controversy in a statement to Fox News Digital, saying her office determined the post could be interpreted differently than intended and removed it.

"A post referencing the death of Charlie Kirk was removed from our account. We recognized the post could be misconstrued, and that's why it came down. We have also addressed this issue internally," Lincoln-Goldfinch said.

HOW CHARLIE KIRK’S ASSASSINATION CHANGED THE WAY CONSERVATIVES APPROACH HOSTILE OPPONENTS

The dispute came as new evidence emerged about the ICE operation that ended with Graces Perez being shot. Surveillance footage published Wednesday showed at least two federal law enforcement vehicles pursuing Graces Perez's vehicle with emergency lights flashing and sirens sounding before the shooting. 

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) confirmed the video's authenticity to Fox News Digital.

Lincoln-Goldfinch has disputed the federal government’s account, saying Garces Perez was working as a DoorDash driver when an unmarked vehicle struck his car and that he did not initially know federal agents were pursuing him. She has also challenged DHS’ characterization of his immigration status.

DHS said Garces Perez is a Venezuelan national who had a final order of removal and was the subject of a targeted vehicle stop. The department also said his work authorization had expired in 2025 and disputed claims about his treatment after the shooting.

"No amount of smears and false narratives will slow down ICE from doing its job to arrest illegal aliens from our communities," DHS said.

AUSTIN ICE SHOOTING SPARKS FIGHT OVER VENEZUELAN ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT'S DEPORTATION

Austin police released body camera footage Tuesday showing officers arriving immediately after the shooting and helping Graces Perez from his vehicle. The video contradicted an earlier claim that federal agents pulled him from the car, although the videos did not capture the shooting itself.

The shooting has also moved into federal court. Lincoln-Goldfinch’s firm filed a lawsuit seeking to prevent Garces Perez’s immediate removal, and a federal judge ordered that he remain in the country so he can appear at a Sept. 30 hearing.

The circumstances surrounding the shooting remain under investigation. Homeland Security Investigations, with assistance from the FBI, is leading the federal investigation, while Austin authorities have also reviewed evidence surrounding the encounter.

Fox News' Louis Casiano and Brooke Taylor contributed to this report.

item.title: AOC's 'Tax the Rich' designer accused of leaving small business with massive charity gala bill
item.description: Aurora James, the designer behind AOC's "Tax the Rich" Met Gala dress, faces a lawsuit alleging she stiffed a small business out of over $1 million.
item.content:encoded:
The fashion designer behind Democratic New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez's "Tax the Rich" Met Gala dress is facing a seven-figure lawsuit accusing her of stiffing the small business she hired to throw her own star-studded charity gala.

According to court documents obtained by Fox News Digital, designer Aurora James, 42, is being sued by event organizer The Gathery Inc. over allegations stemming from unpaid bills after it produced the Fifteen Percent Pledge Gala 2026 at Paramount Studios in Los Angeles earlier this year.

The February bash boasted an attendee list that included Meghan Markle and Kimora Lee Simmons and was held with the intention of raising money for Black business owners.

ANNA WINTOUR REPORTEDLY FACES CALLS TO RETIRE AFTER JOHN GALLIANO MET GALA FIRESTORM: ‘LOST HER TOUCH’

However, a lawsuit filed in New York Supreme Court by The Gathery alleges James, her nonprofit Fifteen Percent Pledge and its fiscal sponsor, Philanthropic Ventures Foundation (PVF), left the planners with the bill.

The plaintiffs are seeking at least $1,082,965 in damages from the three parties, along with contractually owed interest and additional financial damages.

According to court documents, James’ nonprofit allegedly made two initial deposits toward the $1.5 million bill to The Gathery, which produced the annual fundraiser in both 2024 and 2025 without issue, before ceasing all payments in November 2025.

James "personally directed the project and repeatedly induced TGI to continue performing even after payment defaults had begun," the suit states.

PRINCE HARRY SUED BY CHARITY HE FOUNDED IN HONOR OF PRINCESS DIANA

"James approved change orders expanding the scope and cost of the event, signed the Feb. 4, 2026, amendment admitting breach, and assured TGI that payment would be forthcoming — all while knowing, or recklessly disregarding, that 15PP lacked the ability to pay," it continued.

James founded the nonprofit organization in 2020 in response to the murder of George Floyd with a goal of encouraging retailers to dedicate 15% of their storefront’s shelf space to products created by Black-owned businesses.

According to its website, Fifteen Percent Pledge is a self-described "racial equity and economic justice non-profit organization working toward a more equitable economic future."

"Launched in 2020 by Aurora James, the initiative was born from seeing multiple acts of injustice and police brutality in the United States with a lack of accountability for the systemic issues at play," its website states.

DEFEATED PROGRESSIVE ‘SQUAD’ LAWMAKER IN HOT SEAT FOR NON-PROFIT’S MISSING PAPER TRAIL

The ongoing lawsuit is not James’ first time allegedly missing payments.

James, who shares a son with Benjamin Bronfman, son of music executive Edgar Bronfman Jr. and actress Sherry Brewer, was reported in 2021 to have run up tax debts through Cultural Brokerage Agency, the parent company of her Brother Vellies fashion brand, including three open state tax warrants from 2018-19 totaling $14,798 in unpaid employee withholding and 15 warrants since 2015, according to the New York Post.

The company has also reportedly faced multiple legal claims alleging it repeatedly failed to pay worker benefits.

The alleged financial hypocrisy by James, an outspoken activist with deep ties to the fashion world, was noted by both legal and political experts.

"These are still allegations that have to be proven in court, but there’s an undeniable irony in an organization dedicated to supporting small businesses being accused of stiffing one for more than $1 million," former Palm Beach County State Attorney Dave Aronberg told Fox News Digital. 

"If you preach economic fairness, you have to practice it too."

AOC DOUBLES DOWN ON ‘MYTH’ OF EARNING A BILLION DOLLARS, CLAIMS FORTUNES ARE BUILT ON ‘ABUSE’

Kaivon Shroff, a former digital organizer for Hillary Clinton’s campaign, also noted the apparent irony in the allegations against James.

"AOC made Aurora James’s ‘Tax the Rich’ dress one of the defining political images of the Met Gala and excess wealth at a time of great economic inequality, so the irony here is impossible to miss," Shroff told Fox News Digital. 

"James built her public brand around economic justice and supporting Black-owned businesses," he added, noting that she is being sued by a small business.

"That is exactly the kind of contradiction opponents seize on to argue that the politics are performative.

"Movements built around economic fairness and supporting marginalized businesses are so important, and they depend heavily on credibility and goodwill," he added. "When the people most visibly associated with those causes are accused of behaving in ways that seem completely at odds with the message, the damage does not stop with the individual. It gives critics an easy way to discredit the cause itself."

Fox News Digital reached out to James’ attorney for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Reporter's Notebook: Call for a free Iran echoes at the United Nations
item.description: Retired Gen. Keith Kellogg and Ambassador Marc Ginsberg called for Iran sanctions at a rally outside the U.N. General Assembly protesting the Iranian president.
item.content:encoded:
UNITED NATIONS, N.Y. — When Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian addressed the United Nations General Assembly, he portrayed his nation as the victim of American and Israeli terrorism.

But outside the hall, several thousand protesters chanted that he should be arrested for being a terrorist.

"They are terrorists. They must go!" the crowd repeatedly shouted, waving green, white and red flags of the resistance.

THE TOP MOMENTS FROM IRAN PRESIDENT’S TENSE VISIT TO US SOIL AS WAR RAGES

"The president of Iran speaks and lies over and over again. He is a murderer. He is a terrorist," former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani told the gathering.

"It is useless to negotiate with them because they are terrorists, murderers, possibly in some ways insane religious maniacs. This would be like trying to reach an agreement with Hitler."

Various former high-level government officials struck the same tone, slamming the radical Islamic regime they say has savagely oppressed and butchered the Iranian people for decades. Estimates say upward of 20,000 protestors who took to the streets of Iran earlier this year demanding freedom have been murdered by the government. Reports of executions of political prisoners continue each week.

"It is time now to free Iran from the mullahs," Retired Lt. General Keith Kellogg, who has served in both Trump administrations, told the gathering, "You have a road map to a secular, non-nuclear Republic of Iran, one that rejoins the free world as a friend."

TRUMP TO ZERO-IN ON IRAN NUCLEAR THREAT, GAZA PLAN AND UN OVERHAUL IN WORLD STAGE SPEECH

Former U.S. Ambassador Marc Ginsberg urged Congress to pass the Maximum Support Act, legislation that would crack down on Iran's resources, confiscate assets of the government and support internet freedom so the Iranian people could organize and have a voice.

"All you have to do, President Trump, is to provide the funding and the support that we need, the tools the Iranian people need," Ginsberg said. "That is the type of help you promised. That is the type of help you can still provide and bring the United States closer to this exit ramp from this war and to accelerate our speed as Iran's arsenal of democracy."

"The people of Iran have rejected every form of dictatorship, whether religious or monarchical," Maryam Rajavi said in a video message to the rally. She is president-elect of the group that sponsored the protest, the National Council of Resistance of Iran.

"The voice of protest from Iran's oppressed people is being heard. The voice rejects the continued occupation of Iran's seat by religious fanatics," she said, referring to the regime's membership in the world body.

US-BACKED ISRAEL-MOROCCO DEAL DEEPENS ABRAHAM ACCORDS AMID GROWING REGIONAL THREATS

The rally was held over a two-day period, and the message to the United Nations diplomats remained consistent.

"The regime only responds to firmness and decisiveness. And that's why sanctions and putting pressure on Iran has been the only solution in terms of external pressure," Alireza Jafarzadeh, deputy director of the NCRI Washington, D.C., office told Fox News.                                                

"The regime is incapable of reform and change. If they were able, they would have done it a long time ago. The real solution for Iran is change by the people of Iran. They can have any talks, any concessions, none of that is going to change the behavior of the regime.   

"The real Iran is represented by the people of Iran," he added. "The real change has to come from within."

item.title: Florida Gators, Ole Miss Rebels find themselves in good old fashioned 'respect off' ahead of Saturday's game
item.description: Lane Kiffin's Ole Miss Rebels and the Florida Gators are locked in a viral #RespectOff ahead of their top-25 SEC showdown in Gainesville, Florida.
item.content:encoded:
You've probably heard the saying "it just means more in the SEC" at least once or twice in the past several years of watching football.

This means, among other things, that the fanbases for each school are hellbent on talking as much trash as humanly possible.

It doesn't matter if it's at the stadium, in the parking lot, or online, all of these schools hate each other and if they don't have a natural animus towards one another, they'll manufacture one.

FLORIDA GATORS COACH JON SUMRALL SAYS HE WOULDN'T HAVE LEFT TULANE IF HE WASN'T ALLOWED TO COACH PLAYOFF TEAM

That doesn't seem to be the case for one of the more marquee matchups coming down the pike this weekend, though.

The top-five Ole Miss Rebels will travel to Gainesville, Florida, to take on the 21st-ranked Gators, and with so much at stake at such an early point in the season, you would expect both teams and fanbases to be at each other's throats, but it's been anything but toxic.

That's right, folks, we have ourselves a good old-fashioned "respect off" brewing between the Gators and Rebels.

It all started on Monday, when Florida head coach Jon Sumrall was informed at his press conference that the Gators were favored by 3.5 points on Saturday.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

His response: "There's a lot of good drugs out there."

A coach being respectful toward his opponent is nothing out of the ordinary, but Sumrall's goodwill must have trickled down to the fans of both school, because social media turned into a Kumbaya session this whole week.

Look at all that love being spread! They even have a hashtag for it all, #RespectOff!

This is in stark contrast to the vibes from the previous week for both teams.

Ole Miss clearly had an axe to grind against LSU, what with them stealing their old coach and all, and Florida and Auburn, as I documented last week, had a century-old rivalry they needed to revive on social media.

I guess the Gators and Rebels really don't have a lot to be mad at each other about.

Sure, Florida also took a run at Lane Kiffin last fall, and Ole Miss is the team who sparked the now-famous Tim Tebow "promise" after winning in The Swamp back in 2008, but that's in the past.

Clearly we are letting bygones be bygones, and I'm here for it.

It could always be worse. You could be Missouri getting accused by Kansas for being a bunch of evil slave owners.

Then again, whoever loses this game is probably going to be pretty pissed when their SEC Championship and College Football Playoff hopes take a hit, so we will wait and see if the #RespectOff carries over on Sunday.

For now, let's just enjoy this armistice while we can.

item.title: Sheridan Gorman’s mom scorches Dem lawmakers she says refused to hear families of slain Americans
item.description: Sheridan Gorman's mother accused Rep. Pramila Jayapal of dismissing angel families and Rep. Jerry Nadler of napping during sanctuary city testimony.
item.content:encoded:
The mother of Sheridan Gorman sharply criticized Democratic lawmakers who support sanctuary city policies Thursday, calling out several members for their behavior during a recent congressional hearing where she testified about her daughter's tragic death.

Jessica Anne Gorman recounted the March 2026 death of her 18-year-old Loyola University Chicago student during a gathering in Washington, D.C. Top Justice Department and administration officials, including Attorney General Todd Blanche, FBI Director Kash Patel, border czar Tom Homan and drug czar Sara Carter, were on hand to honor the victims of violent crime.

Sheridan Gorman was shot and killed while visiting friends near a pier and lighthouse in Chicago. Jose Medina, a Venezuelan national who entered the U.S. illegally and was previously released after a shoplifting arrest in Chicago, has been charged with her murder.

SHERIDAN GORMAN'S PARENTS SAY PROTECTING CHILDREN FROM FAILED IMMIGRATION POLICIES ISN'T A ONE-PARTY FIGHT

During her remarks, Jessica Gorman criticized Democratic lawmakers who advocate for shielding immigrants in the country illegally from federal immigration enforcement.

She recalled testifying at a House hearing on sanctuary policies, saying she could hear laughter from lawmakers as she spoke about losing her daughter.

"And I thought to myself, ‘Boy, the hits just keep on coming,’" Jessica Gorman said Thursday.

DAD OF GIRL LEFT PERMANENTLY DISABLED IN CRASH WITH ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT RIPS DEMS: ‘I REJECT YOUR SYMPATHY’

She specifically called out Rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash., who had remarked during the hearing that it was the fourth of its kind and that there were "many other things we could be doing."

"We were all insulted by Democrat Representative Jayapal telling me — literally telling me — and all the other angel families in the room ... with disdain on her face, that there's other things they could be doing except listening to four sessions," Jessica Gorman said.

ANGEL FAMILIES PLEAD WITH LEADERS TO 'CHOOSE' AMERICAN CHILDREN OVER PROTECTING ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS

"They give us five minutes to tell our daughter's story," Jessica Gorman added. "Our dead children's story. She listened to four before mine. She didn't want to listen to another. And, honestly, I think she should listen to everyone in this room."

Gorman also accused Rep. Jerry Nadler, D-N.Y., of napping during the proceedings.

Also speaking at the event was Stephen Federico, the father of Logan Federico, who was killed while visiting friends at the University of South Carolina. Stephen voiced intense frustration with the broader criminal justice system.

Alexander Dickey, 30, a career criminal with dozens of prior arrests, is accused of shooting and killing Logan Federico during a home break-in.

"My daughter wasn't killed by an illegal alien," Stephen Federico said. "She was killed by a home-grown American career criminal that we arrested 39 damn times. And he was on the street. Tell me that makes sense.

"Can anyone tell me, please, how a felon like that is left on the street," he added. "It's from fingerprint problems. It's from process problems. It's from weak judges. It's from weak prosecutors."

Fox News Digital has reached out to Jayapal's office for comment.

item.title: Unearthed clip exposes clash between El-Sayed and ex-GOP rival: 'Muslims definitely hate you'
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for Michigan's U.S. Senate race, once fired back at Patrick Colbeck over Muslim Brotherhood allegations.
item.content:encoded:
Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Michigan, once fired back at accusations he might have ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, a group that advocates implementing Muslim code, known as Sharia law, as a legal framework.

"Now, you may not hate Muslims. But I’ll tell you, Muslims definitely hate you," El-Sayed said at a 2018 Michigan gubernatorial forum.

The statement, made in response to a question from Michigan lawmaker Patrick Colbeck about his religious affiliations, demonstrates El-Sayed’s resentment toward efforts to use his Muslim faith as a link to Islamic groups like the Muslim Brotherhood. 

It also shows efforts to address fears that, as a Muslim, he would try to implement Sharia law as the law of the land.

VANCE UNLOADS ON EL-SAYED OVER SHARIA REMARKS: ‘THAT’S NOT MY GRANDPA’S DEMOCRATIC PARTY’

Colbeck was also running for governor at the time.

During the panel, Colbeck focused his criticisms on the Muslim Brotherhood, claiming El-Sayed had ties to the Muslim Students Association (MSA), a group listed as part of a strategy memorandum for North America written by one of the Muslim Brotherhood’s members, Mohamed Akram. 

El-Sayed served as the vice president of the MSA chapter at the University of Michigan during his time there as a senior in 2007, according to College Fix.

"This is very serious stuff, guys. This is about civilization jihad," Colbeck said.

Fox News Digital has not discovered any ties between El-Sayed and the Muslim Brotherhood. Notably, the memorandum lists a wide range of organizations, stretching from the Islamic Book Service to the Association of Muslim Scientists and Engineers, groups that, for their own part, don’t maintain a formal relationship with the Muslim Brotherhood.

Colbeck’s comments prompted the moderator at the 2018 panel to direct a question to El-Sayed directly.

"Is Sharia Law instituted here in the state of Michigan a real concern?" the moderator asked.

El-Sayed took the moment to rebuff Colbeck, stating that he would, if elected, swear an oath to uphold the law of the land and not look to subvert it.

EL-SAYED'S DEFENSE OF SHARIA LAW STANCE SPARKS ONLINE ERUPTION FROM CHRISTIANS, CONSERVATIVES: 'HE'S DONE'

"I solemnly swear to uphold the Constitution of the United States and the Constitution of this state — that’s the oath that if any one of us is elected, we will swear. I take that oath particularly seriously because it guarantees me the right to pray as I choose to pray," El-Sayed said at the time.

"Sharia law is not in question in this state."

While the United States doesn’t list the Muslim Brotherhood as a terrorist organization, other countries like Egypt, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Russia all have, citing the group’s history of armed activity.

The Muslim Brotherhood renounced violence in the 1970s but has continued to advocate for ways to codify Muslim religious beliefs in countries around the world since then.

In a 2012 document, the group issued a statement on Islamic law and national identity.

"That is an integral part of the Muslim Brotherhood’s concept of Islamic law or Sharia, which is the most important issue that preoccupies us and which we seek to establish in society, and for which we have offered our dear brothers for martyrdom, imprisonment and persecution over long decades," the group wrote.

The idea of Muslims using the American election process to implement the Muslim code as the law of the land has raised concerns from lawmakers like Rep. Chip Roy, R-Texas, and others who believe Sharia’s many tenets are incompatible with American culture.

"America is facing a threat that directly attacks our Constitution and our Western values: the spread of Sharia law," Roy said in a 2025 press release.

"From Texas to every state in this constitutional republic, instances of Sharia adherents masquerading as ‘refugees’ — and in many cases, sleeper cells connected to terrorist organizations — are threatening the American way of life. Those who succumb to this political ideology seek to replace our legal system and Constitution. Under Sharia law, there is no freedom of speech, religion or women’s rights."

Elsewhere, an increasing number of Muslim representatives and populations in places like Dearborn, Michigan, have led some critics to argue that a kind of preference or leniency toward Muslim individuals is its own version of implementation.

"America, we have lost this city. This is a city that is no longer up under American laws; we are up under Sharia law. We will not have it anymore," Pastor Lorenzo Sewell, the pastor of 180 Church, said during a town council meeting in Dearborn, calling for the town’s councilmembers to denounce the Muslim code.

According to the 2020 U.S. census, a majority of Dearborn residents reported Middle Eastern or North African ancestry at roughly 54.5%.

EL-SAYED'S AGENDA PUTS ‘PERMANENTLY’ CHANGED AMERICA ON THE LINE IN MICHIGAN SENATE RACE, GOP FIREBRAND WARNS

Fox News Digital is not aware of any proposals from El-Sayed to implement facets of Sharia law. When asked about Sharia law and its implementation in the U.S., a spokesperson for El-Sayed said that would not be his mission as a lawmaker.

"Abdul believes in the separation of church and state. While he personally lives by the rules of his faith, as many Americans of various faiths do, Abdul opposes any effort by any religious community to write their faith laws into the laws of our country," the El-Sayed campaign told the Washington Free Beacon earlier this year.

item.title: Ms Rachel doubles down on Gaza advocacy, targets ‘uncancellable’ celebrities for staying silent
item.description: Ms. Rachel challenged "uncancellable" celebrities on Ilana Glazer's podcast, asking why stars with secure careers won't speak out for Palestinian children.
item.content:encoded:
Children's YouTube star Ms. Rachel doubled down on her Gaza advocacy Thursday, criticizing "uncancellable" celebrities who have stayed silent about Palestinian children and questioning why stars with secure careers would not "risk something" to help save lives.

Accurso, whose full name is Rachel Griffin Accurso, appeared on comedian Ilana Glazer's "It's Open" podcast to directly challenge major celebrities who have avoided taking public positions on the war.

"If you are so famous, and you’re uncancellable, and you’re so famous, and you won’t even say like, ‘Kids in Gaza should have schools, people in Gaza should have hospitals.’ Like you won't say something so basic and like why can't you risk something to help save lives," Accurso said.

MS RACHEL DEFENDS HER ACTIVISM BY POINTING TO MISTER ROGERS' POLITICAL LEGACY ON CHILDREN'S TV

Accurso’s latest remarks came after Rabbi Yaakov Menken, executive vice president of the Coalition for Jewish Values, recently told Fox News Digital that he believed the amount of attention she devotes to Palestinian children compared to children suffering elsewhere was disproportionate. 

"When 0.09% of starving children receive 90% of her attention, something is wrong," Menken said.

Elizabeth Barcohana, the California Republican Party’s Jewish engagement chair, also criticized Accurso in a statement to Fox News Digital last week after the children’s entertainer accused celebrities and leaders who had remained silent about Gaza of applying a racial double standard.

"Ms. Rachel is essentially sanitizing terrorism with false and misleading information to emotionally manipulate her very impressionable following," Barcohana said.

MS RACHEL CLAIMS 'NO ONE NEEDS A BILLION DOLLARS,' ENDORSES DEMOCRATIC PROGRESSIVES ABDUL EL-SAYED, CORI BUSH

Accurso broadened her criticism beyond Gaza during the podcast to other humanitarian issues, saying she was frustrated with prominent figures who did not publicly address them.

"I am really upset that people aren't speaking out about kids in detention and aren't speaking out about Gaza and Sudan and everything," Accurso said.

The conversation began with Glazer raising rapper Mackelmore's removal from Ed Sheeran's U.S. tour following his onstage "Free Palestine" remarks. Accurso dismissed Sheeran by name before broadening her criticism.

Tour promoter Messina Touring Group said multiple venues refused to allow Macklemore to perform, while Sheeran later said the decision to remove the rapper was made by the promoter, not him. Sheeran subsequently addressed the controversy at a Philadelphia concert, condemning the Oct. 7 Hamas attacks while describing the situation in Gaza as catastrophic and unjustifiable.

FORMULA ONE DRIVER LEWIS HAMILTON TELLS MACKLEMORE HE IS ‘STANDING’ IN SOLIDARITY WITH HIM ON PALESTINE

Macklemore later pledged $1 million in tour proceeds to Palestinian aid organizations, a donation Accurso pledged to match as she urged other wealthy celebrities to do the same.

Accurso also repeatedly characterized Israel’s conduct in Gaza as "genocide" during the Glazer interview, saying she believed using the term could help pressure the international community to act.

A U.N. Independent International Commission of Inquiry concluded in June that Israeli authorities and security forces deliberately targeted Palestinian children and said their conduct amounted to genocide and other international crimes. Israel rejected the commission’s conclusions and formally challenged what it called flaws in its composition, mandate and methodology.

A separate genocide case brought by South Africa against Israel remains before the International Court of Justice. The court has issued provisional measures in the case but has not issued a final judgment on whether Israel committed genocide.

item.title: Dolly Parton’s sisters push back on feud rumors after nephew’s legal battle with star's estate erupts
item.description: Dolly Parton's sisters deny family feud claims after manager Danny Nozell won a restraining order against nephew Bryan Seaver over alleged threats.
item.content:encoded:
Dolly Parton’s sisters are shutting down claims of a family feud as tensions surrounding the late country legend’s legacy have spilled into court.

Nearly one month after Parton’s death, her sisters pushed back against reports of infighting within the family, insisting they remain united as a separate legal dispute involving the singer’s longtime manager and nephew resulted in a temporary restraining order.

"I’ll say this and this only: there is no feud within our family," Freida Parton shared Wednesday on Instagram. "No one among the Parton/Owens family is fighting over Dolly’s estate. We all love Bryan, just as we all love each other. I love you all!!"

DOLLY PARTON’S SISTER REVEALS ‘LAST THING’ COUNTRY LEGEND ASKED OF HER BEFORE DEATH

Parton's sister Stella echoed Freida's message, emphasizing that the family remains united as it continues to navigate its grief.

"It has been a comfort to experience such an outpouring of love on [Dolly's] behalf as we grieve her passing," Stella posted Thursday on Instagram. 

"We are also grieving the loss of our brother Denver who passed less than a month before her. All families have the same struggles since we are all living in this world having a human experience!

"We are still intact and moving forward because our children and grandchildren look to us for strength and guidance during this difficult time of loss and confusion for them as well," she added. 

"Regardless of what you may have seen on different news outlets, we are all doing what you would be doing under the same circumstances, we are living our lives one day at a time and being grateful for every blessing."

Parton’s legacy took a dramatic turn this week when her longtime manager sought a restraining order against the country icon’s nephew.

Danny Nozell, who runs She's Alive, LLC, an entity Parton created to oversee her business interests, filed for the restraining order on behalf of She's Alive against Bryan Seaver and Seaver's private security company, Squadron Augmented Protection Services, in Nashville, according to The Associated Press.

A Tennessee judge granted the temporary restraining order Wednesday, citing a pattern of alleged threats and demands for payment, along with Seaver’s "claimed access to weapons, experience with violence, and intention to retaliate." The order called the communications "concerning" and specifically pointed to an alleged threat to use force.

Nozell and She's Alive accused Seaver of sending increasingly threatening messages in the weeks leading up to their request for a temporary restraining order. The filing came after She’s Alive fired Seaver over his alleged "terrorizing conduct."

Court documents obtained by The Associated Press show text messages and emails allegedly sent by Seaver.

In one message written Sept. 1 and included in the court documents, Seaver said, "I’m going to set up a podcast dedicated to ruining Dolly’s brand partnerships and telling the violations these people have done on us. It’s going to be great. Or f---ing pay me."

Seaver pushed back against the allegations in a statement shared with TMZ. He said the messages had been taken out of context to make them appear threatening.

Seaver's company, Squadron Augmented Protection Services, had provided Parton’s security detail throughout her career. Parton chose Seaver to publicly announce her death. The singer-songwriter died Aug. 25.

item.title: What's on the menu for Trump's state dinner with China's Xi? One American staple is notably missing
item.description: President Donald Trump's state dinner with Xi Jinping features a pescatarian menu with sesame-crusted sea bass and White House honey dessert.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump, despite his wealth, isn't exactly known for his refined palette.

But Thursday's state dinner with Chinese President Xi Jinping will be an elegant affair, and a far cry from the 47th president's notorious McDonald's order of two Big Macs, two Filet-O-Fish sandwiches and a large chocolate shake. The swanky event will be quite the opposite.

Conspicuously missing from the menu, however, is an American dining staple — red meat. 

In fact, no meat will be served at all. Instead, the dinner is exclusively a pescatarian affair.

TRUMP-XI SUMMIT COULD HOLD KEY TO LOWER GAS PRICES, GOP CHAIRMAN SAYS

The menu for the event, provided to Fox News Digital by First Lady Melania Trump's office, says the first course consists of yellow squash velouté, wild mushroom fricassée, crispy pancetta and scallion oil.

"The first course offers a refined and silky-smooth velouté made of sweet yellow squash," the menu states. "This course is gently blended to highlight its delicate seasonal flavors of earthy wild mushrooms, sautéed with fresh herbs. Together, these ingredients create a rich fricassee, complemented by crispy pancetta for a savory and smoky contrast. A finishing drizzle of scallion oil adds vibrance and a subtle allium brightness to the dish."

TRUMP HOSTS KING CHARLES, QUEEN CAMILLA AT WHITE HOUSE STATE DINNER: FASHION, FOOD AND A STANDOUT GIFT

Served next is a sesame crusted sea bass with braised bok choy, roasted garden eggplant and a French green herb sauce.

"The second course is prepared delicately with fresh seabass and coated in toasted sesame seeds," according to the menu.

"This combination creates a fragrant nutty crust while keeping the fish tender. The fish is served with crisp baby bok choy and roasted garden eggplant, creating lightly caramelized flavors. The dish is finished with a vibrant sauce verte of fresh herbs, which add brightness, acidity, and a garden character."

The two heads of state and their guests will enjoy vanilla crémeux and White House honey iced cream, walnut frangipane and sour cherry confit for their final course.

DAUGHTER OF CHINESE UYGHUR PRISONER MAKES EMOTIONAL PLEA TO TRUMP DURING SPOTLIGHT XI SUMMIT

"The dessert course is a smooth vanilla crémeux with a vibrant sour cherry confit center, set a top a rich walnut frangipane," the menu says. "The dessert’s fruit shaped form is complimented by a delicate ice cream made with harvested White House honey."

The First Lady unveiled a beehive on the White House South Lawn earlier this year.

Famous American tenor Christopher Macchio, who was featured at the Republican National Convention in Dallas a few weeks ago, will entertain for the evening, along with military musicians from the Army and the Marine Corps.

"The décor for the evening is an expression of warmth and celebration and draws on the color red’s longstanding cultural significance throughout Chinese history," the First Lady's memo says, and will feature "urns overflowing with red blossoms and tables covered by red linen with dahlias and ranunculus."

After the dinner, both presidents are expected to retire for the evening.

Friday, Trump will take Xi on an expedition to the National Archives before the communist leader departs the United States mid-afternoon.

item.title: Dale Earnhardt once broke his hand punching a man who killed a deer on his North Carolina farm
item.description: Dale Earnhardt Jr. recounts the wild story of his dad tackling and punching a trespasser who snuck onto his North Carolina farm to shoot a deer.
item.content:encoded:
Dale Earnhardt wasn't called "The Intimidator" for nothing. But as it turns out, the seven-time NASCAR Cup Series champion didn't reserve all that intimidation for the racetrack.

Just ask the guy who decided to sneak onto his property and shoot one of his deer.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

During Wednesday's episode of "The Dale Jr. Download," Dale Earnhardt Jr. recalled the time his dad broke his hand punching a man who killed a deer on his North Carolina farm.

And while Earnhardt Sr. certainly wasn't afraid of a confrontation on the track, his son said he couldn't recall his dad ever getting into an actual fight with another driver.

The deer incident, though… that was a different story.

According to Dale Jr., the whole thing started back in 1993 when a man working on a tractor on Earnhardt's property spotted some deer.

Later that afternoon, the man went to a bar with a buddy and started telling him about the animals he'd seen. And, as tends to happen when alcohol enters the equation, the two came up with a brilliant idea.

They'd sneak back onto Earnhardt's property and shoot themselves a deer.

"The more they drank, the braver they got," Earnhardt Jr. recalled.

So, around dark, the two men hopped the fence and made their way onto the property.

What they didn't know was that Earnhardt and his farm manager happened to be walking along a power line nearby.

The two heard a gunshot and watched as a wounded deer ran down the clearing before collapsing. Rather than immediately confronting the trespassers, Earnhardt and his farm manager hid in the tree line and waited for the men to come retrieve the animal.

CHASE BRISCOE SAYS DEER HUNTING GIVES HIM A BIGGER RUSH THAN DRIVING 200MPH IN NASCAR

And when they showed up, The Intimidator lived up to his nickname.

According to Dale Jr., his dad charged the man carrying the gun, tackled him and began punching him in the face.

He hit the guy so hard that he broke his own hand.

Earnhardt eventually recognized the man's voice and realized he was the same guy who had been working on his tractor earlier that day. He then held the man until police arrived.

Talk about a bad day at work.

Earnhardt wasn't upset because someone had stolen a deer he was planning to hunt himself. He just liked having the animals around.

According to his son, Earnhardt had some impressive bucks roaming his property, but he wasn't interested in shooting them. He enjoyed watching them and wanted to keep them around.

And he certainly didn't want word getting out that his farm was home to some big deer.

So when Earnhardt showed up to the 1993 NASCAR awards banquet sporting a cast on his broken hand, he made up a different explanation for the injury.

"He didn't want people to know about his deer," Dale Jr. explained. "He didn't want more people showin' up, trying to sneak into his property."

Earnhardt even had a black-and-white cast to match his tuxedo as he accepted his sixth Cup Series championship trophy.

But the broken hand created another problem when the 1994 racing season rolled around.

According to Junior, his dad was told he wouldn't be allowed to compete in the Daytona 500 while wearing the cast. So Earnhardt cut it off himself.

Problem solved.

Anyway, let that be a lesson to you. Don't go hunting on private land without permission. It just doesn't turn out well — not for you, not for the deer, and not even for the landowner who has to knock your lights out.

SOROS-BACKED DA'S LAX ILLEGAL IMMIGRATION POLICIES LED TO 'PREVENTABLE' BUS STOP STABBING MURDER: COMPLAINT

The Department of Homeland Security says Jalloh, a Sierra Leone national who entered the U.S. illegally in 2012, has been arrested more than 30 times. His previous charges included rape, malicious wounding, assault and theft, DHS said.

SANCTUARY COUNTY REFUSED 615 ICE TRANSFER REQUESTS, TURNED OVER JUST 11 ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS, RECORDS SHOW

"Thirty times the system had a chance to stop him. Thirty times," she wrote. "I think about that every single day."

JORDAN GRILLS SOROS-BACKED DA DESCANO IN HEATED SPAT OVER SOFT-ON-CRIME POLICY: 'THIS IS ALMOST LAUGHABLE'

Cheryl questioned why Jalloh was released after an arrest she recalled from the winter before Stephanie's death. The details of that case and who made the release decision have not been independently confirmed.

"When you let these people back out on the streets, they're not gonna stop. Why would they stop?" she said.

Cheryl Minter also pointed to Descano's 2020 plea bargaining policy. It advised prosecutors to "consider immigration consequences where possible" and weigh how charges could affect a defendant's immigration status, WTOP reported. The outlet reported in May that the webpage detailing the policy was no longer publicly available on Descano's office website. Cheryl Minter argues that prosecutors should put public safety first.

That policy is under federal scrutiny. The Justice Department announced in May it was investigating whether Descano's office gave defendants who are in the country illegally preferential treatment over U.S. citizens in charging decisions and plea deals. The department said it had reached no conclusions. The investigation does not establish how Jalloh's earlier cases were handled.

SOROS-BACKED PROSECUTOR SET FOR CAPITOL HILL GRILLING AS SANCTUARY POLICIES FACE RECKONING

Descano defended the policy after receiving notice of the investigation. 

"My policies are fair, legal, and reflect the values of my community," he wrote in a post on X.

Asked what she wants from her petition, Cheryl Minter said her priority is changing those practices in Fairfax County and beyond. She also wants Descano out of office.

SOROS-BACKED DA ACCUSED OF GOING EASY ON ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS GETS SQUEEZED BY HOUSE GOP

"I think, first and foremost, is the change," she said. "Second would be, I would love to see Descano out."

Jennifer Harrison, executive director of the Victims' Rights Reform Council, helped Cheryl Minter start the Change.org petition. Cheryl Minter said she knows an online petition cannot itself remove Descano but hopes it will drive scrutiny of his office.

Congress is also pressing Descano for answers. House Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, subpoenaed him Sept. 16 as part of an investigation into whether prosecutors give preferential treatment to criminal suspects because of their immigration status.

Jordan set a Sept. 25 deadline after accusing Descano's office of failing to fully comply with earlier requests.

In a previous statement to Fox News Digital, Descano's office called the subpoena a "needless escalation" and accused the committee of waging a "partisan siege" against Fairfax County. It said the office had turned over more than 1,100 pages of documents, that Descano had voluntarily testified and that it would continue to respond to legitimate inquiries while working to keep the county safe.

The office has separately said it is prosecuting Jalloh for Stephanie's murder with a trial scheduled for January 2027 and cannot comment further on the pending case.

WATCH: SOROS PROSECUTOR’S HEARING DEVOLVES INTO ANGRY CHAOS OVER ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT RAPE CASE: 'BE QUIET!'

Fairfax County police said Jalloh was arrested after an employee at a local business recognized him and called authorities the day after Stephanie Minter was killed. He was held without bond.

ICE lodged a detainer on Feb. 25 after Jalloh was in custody, asking to be notified before his release, according to DHS. The agency said it had also lodged a detainer against him in 2020 and that an immigration judge later ordered him removed to a country other than Sierra Leone.

Cheryl Minter said employees of Descano's office working on her daughter's murder case have been "wonderful with me." She said her criticism is aimed at the decisions she believes left a repeat offender free.

"I want people never to stop talking about it," she said. "I just don't want the talk to stop, and I'll do whatever to keep it going."

"Stephanie cannot speak for herself anymore. So I am," she wrote in the petition.

Fox News Digital reached out to Descano's office for comment on Cheryl Minter's allegations and petition.

Fox News Digital's Elizabeth Elkind contributed to this report.

item.title: Strokes nearly double among adults under a certain age in disturbing trend
item.description: Stroke incidence among young adults more than doubled over three decades, with ischemic stroke and marijuana use surging, a new study reveals.
item.content:encoded:
Stroke incidence more than doubled among young adults in a recent study.

Researchers at the University of Cincinnati analyzed data from 2,076 first-ever strokes among adults ages 20–54 in the Greater Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky region from 1993-1994 to 2020.

Over those three decades, the incidence increased from about 34 to 62 strokes per 100,000 people per year.

HEART ATTACKS AND STROKES RISING WITH EXTREME WEATHER EVENTS, RESEARCH SUGGESTS

The increase was primarily driven by ischemic stroke, which occurs when a blood vessel supplying the brain becomes blocked.

Among the younger adults who experienced strokes, there was an increase in hypertension, diabetes, atrial fibrillation (irregular heartbeat) and substance use.

"This has major implications, since young people who develop disability from a stroke may no longer be able to work or provide for their families," study co-author David J. Robinson, M.D., an assistant professor of clinical neurology and rehabilitation medicine at the University of Cincinnati College of Medicine, told Fox News Digital.

"We don't know for sure why strokes are becoming more common, and we really need to study this in more depth if we are going to reverse this trend."

8 COMMON FOOD PRESERVATIVES LINKED TO HIGHER RISK OF HIGH BLOOD PRESSURE AND HEART DISEASE

There was also a sharp increase in documented substance use, which rose from 4.6% to 40.2% in the study period, primarily marijuana.

"It's hard to say whether this is responsible for any of the rise in stroke; there is a relationship between marijuana use and stroke, but most of the evidence is with heavier use," Robinson said. "The relationship between marijuana use and cardiovascular disease needs more study so that we can properly advise our patients."

In contrast to younger adults, stroke rates declined among older adults, falling from about 619 to 453 strokes per 100,000 people per year.

Short-term survival after stroke also improved, the researchers found. The share of younger adults who died within 30 days of a stroke declined from 11.7% to 9.4% – primarily for bleeding-related strokes, including intracerebral and subarachnoid hemorrhages.

WHAT TO DO IF SOMEONE IS HAVING A STROKE, AFTER JILL BIDEN REVEALED DEBATE-NIGHT FEARS

"Our study might provide evidence that we have gotten better at treating people who have hemorrhagic strokes and helping them survive, which is encouraging," said Robinson. "Still, prevention is the most important thing to focus on, because just surviving a stroke doesn't mean you aren't left without disability."

The findings were published in the journal Neurology on Sept. 23.

Dr. Jason A. Gluck, vice chair of the Heart & Vascular Institute and system chief of cardiology at AtlantiCare in New Jersey, noted that while stroke is still uncommon in young adults, that doesn’t mean they have zero risk.

"The concerning findings in this particular trial is that stroke rates are moving in the wrong direction for the younger population," Gluck, who was not involved in the research, told Fox News Digital.

"While many of the risk factors are things that we can identify and treat before a stroke occurs, when you're young, sometimes you don't know about it – so awareness is key."

Risk factors are pervasive across all age groups, the doctor noted.

POPULAR ARTIFICIAL SWEETENER LINKED TO POTENTIALLY DANGEROUS HEART RISK

"The same things that happen to 70-year-olds can happen at 40 – if you have high blood pressure, if you have diabetes, if you’re smoking, if there's obesity, abnormal cholesterol and activity, all those things can lead to [stroke]," he warned.

"Vascular disease doesn't suddenly begin when you're 65; it develops over time."

The main limitation of the study is that it did not include comparable risk factors for people without stroke.

"We can't say for sure how many of the stroke risk factors are changing in people without stroke in our region," Robinson noted. "This makes it really hard to determine what is causing this rising incidence. We will need to look in other studies to really understand the ‘why’ of this trend."

Also, the findings may have been affected by changes in medical documentation and diagnostic methods over the nearly three decades. One example provided was an increase in MRI use, which could potentially improve the detection of stroke. It was also possible that the rise in substance use was due to increased documentation or disclosure.

The study was also geographically limited, including just five counties in one U.S. state.

"While stroke is still relatively uncommon in younger individuals, it can happen and be really devastating," Robinson said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The doctor emphasized that hypertension is the risk factor most tightly associated with stroke.

"Younger people may not have a lot of opportunities to get their blood pressure and other risk factors screened, and we need to come up with solutions that can meet them where they are," he said.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Robinson recommended using the American Heart Association’s "Life’s Essential 8," which is a checklist for optimizing your cardiovascular health.

"It includes blood pressure control along with eating better, being less sedentary, quitting any tobacco products, sleeping well, managing your weight, controlling cholesterol and managing blood sugar."

Gluck recommends using the "BE FAST" guide to determine whether someone may be having a stroke, as follows.

"If you're having these symptoms or your loved one is having these symptoms, don't drive yourself to the hospital," he advised. "Call 911. Be fast."
